terminal_findings.mechanism: Canonical-oriented consumers could ignore occurrence-level severity because materiality was excluded from the deduplication key and lacked group aggregation.
terminal_findings.precondition: A low-materiality occurrence is canonical for a deduplication group.
terminal_findings.event: A severe occurrence with the same deduplication identity arrives.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Triage retains the canonical occurrence's low severity and under-prioritizes the group.
terminal_findings.falsifier: A monotonic group maximum, mandatory consumer contract, escalation event, and low-to-severe propagation test.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Cross-revision identity originally trusted an unchanged axis and mechanism ID despite changed observable behavior.
terminal_findings.precondition: A revision retains its mechanism ID.
terminal_findings.event: P1 changes STORE_UNAVAILABLE handling from quarantine to durable journal and replay.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: A concern about the new handler can be marked duplicate of a concern about the old handler.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Behavioral fingerprints and versions separate changed handlers, while inconsistent same-version fingerprints become INDETERMINATE_IDENTITY.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Immutable occurrences originally lacked append-only correction, supersession, and temporal-authority semantics.
terminal_findings.precondition: An earlier classification or canonical linkage is later found incorrect.
terminal_findings.event: A rebuild or adjudication changes the authoritative classification.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Auditors cannot deterministically reconstruct the authoritative association for a requested time.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Append-only DECIDED and SUPERSEDED events with causality, bitemporal projections, integrity constraints, and deterministic replay tests.

terminal_findings.mechanism: P1 defines monotonic maximum group materiality, but P3 does not define membership and de-escalation after supersession, removal, or reassignment.
terminal_findings.precondition: A severe occurrence has escalated a group's materiality.
terminal_findings.event: Its authoritative classification is superseded, removed, or moved to another group.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Current-view consumers continue reporting severe materiality unsupported by any live group member.
terminal_findings.falsifier: View-specific projection tests derive materiality from live classifications with defined correction and de-escalation, or separate historical maximum from current severity.

terminal_findings.mechanism: The earliest-accepted canonical rule lacks a total immutable ordering and atomic repair semantics for affected source and destination groups.
terminal_findings.precondition: A group has multiple accepted occurrences and an established canonical member.
terminal_findings.event: The canonical is corrected out, or a backdated earlier member enters or moves between groups.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Consumers observe a stale or non-member canonical, incorrect materiality, or divergent replay results.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Define a total immutable ordering and atomically recompute canonical identity and materiality for both affected groups, with reassignment, rejection, and backdating tests.

terminal_findings.mechanism: Backdated supersession lacks complete interval-admissibility and two-dimensional effective-time/known-time selection rules.
terminal_findings.precondition: An authoritative event already begins at a later effective time.
terminal_findings.event: A subsequently recorded replacement is assigned an earlier effective time.
terminal_findings.observable_failure: Authority intervals become invalid or conflicting, causing effective-time and known-time projections to disagree or fail.
terminal_findings.falsifier: Specify interval-validity and effective-at/known-at selection rules that pass before-predecessor, equal-time tie, and repeated-rebuild tests.

limitations: Closed-world run; no external evidence or unrelated workspace inspection was used.
Three separate fresh core threads were used: /root/proposing_tl, /root/peer_tl, and /root/chief_architect; no specialists were added.
Peer received no proposal before its first activated inspection. Chief received only a readiness contract before its blind terminal scan, then received the full record for reconciliation.

The three-cycle ceiling was reached. FINDING-4 and both blind-Chief findings remain open and require normative projection, canonical-repair, interval-boundary, and deterministic-rebuild gates before release.
